type: criminal prosecution (subsidy fraud, damage to EU financial interests)
description: Prosecutors allege that in 2007 the Čapí hnízdo farm and conference centre in Central Bohemia was moved out of the Agrofert group and its ownership concealed through anonymous shares so that it could obtain a CZK 50 million (about EUR 2 million) EU-co-financed subsidy reserved for small and medium-sized enterprises. Babiš was charged in October 2017 and indicted with his former adviser Jana Nagyová (now an ANO MEP) on 21 March 2022 for subsidy fraud and damaging the financial interests of the European Union. Babiš denies the charges and describes the case as politically motivated. The subsidy was repaid voluntarily in 2018 by the company that owns the complex, according to Czech reporting.
outcome: No final verdict as to Babiš. The Municipal Court in Prague acquitted Babiš and Nagyová on 9 January 2023 and again on 14 February 2024; the High Court in Prague annulled both acquittals (September 2023 and 23 June 2025), the second time with a binding legal opinion that the conduct amounted to subsidy fraud and damage to the EU's financial interests. Babiš regained immunity on his re-election as an MP in October 2025; the court's request of 9 October 2025 to release him was refused by the Chamber of Deputies on 5 March 2026. On 12 March 2026 the court severed his part of the case, which cannot continue for the duration of his current parliamentary mandate. In the separated case Nagyová was convicted on 4 May 2026 (three-year suspended sentence, five years' probation, CZK 500,000 fine); the High Court upheld the verdict on 31 August 2026, making it final, and her lawyer announced an extraordinary appeal (dovolání) to the Supreme Court.
court: Municipal Court in Prague (Městský soud v Praze); appeals: High Court in Prague (Vrchní soud v Praze)
presumption_note: Andrej Babiš has not been convicted and is presumed innocent. He was acquitted twice at first instance; both acquittals were annulled on appeal and no verdict on his guilt has been delivered. As of October 2026 the proceedings against him are suspended because the Chamber of Deputies refused consent to prosecution, which under the Czech Constitution bars prosecution only for the duration of his current mandate. The final conviction of co-defendant Jana Nagyová does not establish his guilt. He denies the charges.
key_facts: Charges: subsidy fraud and damage to the financial interests of the EU; OLAF also investigated the subsidy (final report December 2017).
The Chamber lifted his immunity in this case in 2017, 2018 and 2022, but refused in March 2026.

High Court ruling of 23 June 2025: the evidence taken allows no other conclusion than that the defendants acted purposefully; the written reasons, published in August 2025, found that both committed subsidy fraud and damaged the EU's financial interests.

Under the court's decision the case against Babiš can resume when his current mandate ends; if he is re-elected, the court would have to ask the newly elected Chamber for consent again (ČT24). Novinky expects no resolution before the 2029 election.

case: French money-laundering investigation over the Château Bigaud purchase
description: Following the Pandora Papers revelations of October 2021, French authorities opened an investigation, reported by Le Monde as starting in February 2022, into whether Babiš laundered the proceeds of tax fraud in connection with the 2009 purchase of the Château Bigaud estate in Mougins through offshore companies; suspected concealment of the real owner and tax evasion were also examined. The inquiry was conducted by the Central Office against Corruption and Financial and Tax Offences (OCLCIFF) for the National Financial Prosecutor's Office (PNF). Babiš says the purchases complied with the law.
outcome: No charges. On 12 May 2026 the PNF told Seznam Zprávy that investigators had completed their work and returned the file to the prosecutor, who will decide on further steps; their findings were not disclosed. Seznam Zprávy noted that as a serving head of government Babiš enjoys immunity from prosecution in France while in office. This profile found no report of a prosecutorial decision as of October 2026.
court: Parquet national financier (National Financial Prosecutor's Office), Paris
presumption_note: Babiš has not been charged in France or elsewhere in connection with the purchase and is presumed innocent. He has not been acquitted either, because no charge has been brought; the matter is at the investigation stage and its findings are not public. He denies any wrongdoing.
key_facts: Investigators described Babiš as the only suspect in the money-laundering inquiry, according to Seznam Zprávy.
ICIJ noted in 2022 that the alleged facts are old and may be time-barred.
French prosecutors sent requests for international legal assistance, some of which had been answered by 2023 (iROZHLAS).

case: Babiš v. Slovak Nation's Memory Institute / Slovak Republic (StB registration)
description: In 2012 Babiš sued the Slovak Nation's Memory Institute (ÚPN) seeking a ruling that he was wrongly registered in Czechoslovak State Security (StB) records as an agent with the code name 'Bureš'. A Bratislava district court ruled in his favour in June 2014 and the regional court upheld this in 2015, but the Slovak Constitutional Court annulled those rulings in 2017. In later rounds the courts held that ÚPN was the wrong defendant and that he should have sued the Slovak Republic represented by the Interior Ministry (Regional Court Bratislava, 14 June 2022; Supreme Court, 31 August 2023); the Constitutional Court rejected his complaint on 1 February 2024.
outcome: In October 2024 the Slovak Interior Ministry concluded a settlement with Babiš, approved by the Bratislava IV Municipal Court, in which the ministry stated that he had been wrongly registered and had not knowingly cooperated with the StB; Babiš waived claims for damages and withdrew his applications to the European Court of Human Rights. ÚPN, which was not a party, says the settlement creates no obligations for it and continues to list him as an agent (statement of 4 June 2025).
court: Slovak courts (District and Regional Court Bratislava, Supreme Court, Constitutional Court); settlement approved by the Municipal Court Bratislava IV
presumption_note: A civil dispute about archival records, not a criminal case: no court has found Babiš guilty of any offence in connection with the StB. The settlement reflects the position of the Slovak Interior Ministry; the ÚPN maintains its listing. Babiš denies having knowingly collaborated.
key_facts: Earlier rulings were overturned by the Slovak Constitutional Court in 2017 and 2019.
The ministry cited two legal analyses indicating a high risk of losing the case and possible damages claims.
Czech Prime Minister Petr Fiala called the settlement a 'political deal'.

case: Seznam.cz v. Andrej Babiš (protection of reputation)
description: On 3 March 2026 the Czech internet company Seznam.cz announced a civil suit against Babiš for protection of the good reputation of a legal entity, over his repeated public claims that the company avoided about CZK 900 million in withholding tax on dividends and that its news services Seznam Zprávy and Novinky.cz publish lies and manipulation. Seznam seeks the deletion of social-media posts, a ban on repeating the claims and an apology. Babiš said he stands by his statements.
outcome: Pending; no ruling had been reported in the sources consulted as of October 2026.
court: Czech civil court (court not named in public reporting)
presumption_note: A civil claim, not a criminal case. Neither side's allegations have been tested in court; Babiš disputes the claim.
key_facts: Seznam says it asked Babiš at the end of 2025 to stop the statements before suing.
Seznam says the company has always been seated in the Czech Republic and its owner is a Czech tax resident.
